L
2(x + 3)
Right expression
R
2x + 6
What makes an identity?

Both expressions have the same coefficient of x², of x and of 1. Then they agree for every possible x.

One matching value is not enough

Two different polynomials might be equal for one x. Compare every coefficient, or find a counterexample.

COMPARE
Build both tile mats to compare.
Do both sides mean the same?

IDENTITY WORKSHOP
QUESTION 4
Compare the two expressions
Left expression
L
(x + 2)(x + 3)
Right expression
R
x² + 5x + 6
What makes an identity?

Both expressions have the same coefficient of x², of x and of 1. Then they agree for every possible x.

One matching value is not enough

Two different polynomials might be equal for one x. Compare every coefficient, or find a counterexample.

COMPARE
Build both tile mats to compare.
Do both sides mean the same?
